I will keep to the crop pattern I know best in Quzhou: winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land. That is the most practical choice for me because it matches our local climate on the North China Plain, I already understand the field work well, and it gives me two harvests in one year. I do not want to spread my effort into unfamiliar cash crops, because I have primary-school education and I would rather do steady work I can manage confidently with local seed dealers, machinery, and buyers. Wheat is my main grain crop through spring into early summer, and after I harvest it I will sow maize immediately so I do not lose the season.

For management, I will stay with straightforward field practices. I will use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed because I want stable emergence and yield, not risky seed I save myself. For wheat, I will prepare the land with rotary tillage, put on enough nitrogen first and then topdress, irrigate about three times if water allows, and spray twice mainly for weeds and disease. After wheat harvest, I will seed maize quickly with no-tillage on the wheat stubble to save time and moisture. I will give maize more nitrogen than phosphorus, irrigate twice in the key growth stages, and spray about twice for weeds and insects. My goal is not to chase the very highest yield, but to get a stable harvest with work I know I can finish on time.
